items.claim: Governments spend about US$11 trillion a year on public procurement, about 12% of global GDP (2018 data).
items.source: World Bank, Bosio & Djankov, 'How large is public procurement?'

items.claim: Open Contracting Partnership and Spend Network estimate about US$13 trillion a year in public contracts.
Global factoring volume reached EUR 4.039 trillion in 2025.
Duplicated warehouse receipts were used to borrow repeatedly against the same metal; bank loans above US$1.7bn; founder sentenced to 23 years.
US prosecutors allege fake, inflated and double-pledged invoices were submitted to factoring partners; Chapter 11 with over US$9bn of liabilities and about US$2.3bn of factoring liabilities.
Executives allegedly pledged the same collateral to several lenders (about US$2.2bn pledged against about US$1.4bn real); two executives pleaded guilty.
The Swiss regulator found Credit Suisse could not check whether receivables financed through Greensill funds were actually owed; 72% of one sub-fund's exposure came from future receivables.
Italy's average public payment time fell from about 120-130 days (2013) to 30 days (2024) after the central invoice platform (PCC).
items.source: MEF/RGS data via Il Sole 24 Ore

items.claim: India's MSME Samadhaan portal holds 256,892 delayed-payment applications worth INR 55,244 crore, INR 20,979 crore still pending.
items.source: CRISIL press release citing the portal

items.claim: Peru Compras recorded 154,400 purchase orders on the IDB's LACChain; earlier pilots (Colombia, Chile) stamped documents for transparency but none enforced single financing or statutory caps.
items.source: Andina; WEF via Global Government Forum

items.claim: Public authorities must pay within 30 days, extendable to 60 for public healthcare.
The Court of Justice ruled Italy breached the 30/60-day rule for public authorities.
The European Commission attributes one in four EU bankruptcies to late payment.
items.source: Accountancy Europe factsheet on the Late Payment Regulation proposal

items.claim: A framework agreement must determine at the outset the maximum volume; once that limit is reached the agreement has no further effect.
items.source: CJEU C-216/17 Antitrust and Coopservice, paras. 60-61

items.claim: The notice must state a maximum quantity or value; it may be split among participating authorities.
items.source: CJEU C-23/20 Simonsen & Weel, operative part 1 and paras. 78-79

items.claim: 10 of 11 task orders (over US$66M) placed by one agency for another on a shared GSA contract were outside its scope; GAO designated interagency contracting a high-risk area.
Brazilian public procurement averaged 12.5% of GDP in 2006-2016.

Price-registration procedures from Jan 2023 to Jun 2025 totalled about R$ 970.9bn in 301.5k procurements run on 179 different systems (federal systems: R$ 337.8bn); in 2025 they were R$ 470bn (42.38% of R$ 1.1tn). The federal adhesion module allowed requests and authorizations above the 2x cap (balances of -2, -155, -25), rounded the 50% cap up, allowed authorization after expiry, and could not produce reliable remaining balances.
62 bodies adhered to a R$ 32 million Ministry of Health record, a theoretical exposure of about R$ 1.984 billion; TCU ordered limits on adhesions.
items.source: TCU Acórdão 1.487/2007-Plenário, as quoted in secondary sources (original not reachable online)

items.claim: The national associations of courts of accounts recommend checking limits before accepting adhesions and publishing registered quantities, contracts and balances per item.

Payments follow chronological order per funding source and category; deviations need prior justification in five listed cases and monthly publication; unjustified deviation is a crime (CP art. 337-H).
More than two months of payment delay entitles the supplier to suspend performance or terminate.
Federal unpaid committed expenditure (restos a pagar) carried into 2026: R$ 391.5bn (9.4% of the budget), of which R$ 109.0bn already processed (delivered and verified).
items.source: Tesouro Nacional, Relatório de Restos a Pagar 2026

items.claim: Federal suppliers may borrow up to 70% of what remains on a contract; follow-ons only with the same bank; the body pays into the linked account; no published operation volumes found.

Registered card receivables are partitioned by authorized registries so the same receivable is not negotiated twice; electronic duplicatas (Lei 13.775/2018) launched in 2026 with the same aim. Government contract receivables are not covered by either.
items.source: Banco Central do Brasil (Res. CMN 4.734/2019); B3

items.claim: Alagoas regulates price registration closely following the federal decree, mandates the federal Gestão de Atas tool (art. 24) and forbids state bodies from adhering to non-capital municipal records (art. 33).
An Alagoas central purchasing body record was adhered to by a police force of another state, showing state records circulate across jurisdictions.
items.source: Termo de Adesão à Ata nº 693/2025 (PMGO)

items.claim: Federal prosecutors demanded that the State of Alagoas regularize transfers to an oncology hospital serving 47 municipalities, late since November 2024 (health transfers, not ordinary supplier purchases).
Several Alagoas and Pernambuco municipalities bought robotics kits by adhering to the same few municipal records; TCU suspended new federal transfers for the kits (Acórdão 914/2022).
338 of 643 São Paulo municipalities (52.6%) adhered to other entities' records; 22.5% of them without a preliminary study showing the adhesion was advantageous.
51 municipalities bought interactive screens from one supplier (about R$ 152M); one record was reused by at least 10 cities; audit estimated unit price about R$ 10k against R$ 32k paid.
items.source: TCE-RS audit as reported by Extra Classe

items.claim: TCE-SP suspended R$ 7.7M of payments for school uniforms bought by adhering to another state's consortium record.
1,202 of 4,172 responding municipalities (28.8%) were behind on supplier payments; 31% expected to carry bills into 2026 without cash.

At a state central purchasing body: one adhesion is recorded in the electronic process, in Compras.gov.br and in an internal control system or spreadsheets; supplier acceptance arrives by e-mail and is attached as PDF; an adhesion took 51 days from request to authorization; the 50% cap is rounded down; authorizations are rectified after budget review; balances are reserved and later written off or restored.
items.source: Founder's operational knowledge (anonymized; internal documents not published)
